newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended mixed, with longer maturities showing small losses, in a market largely devoid of investor interest, dealers said.
"It's just typical pre-Christmas doldrums now," one broker said. "All the damage has already been done by U.S. Treasuries and I can't see things picking up again before the new year."
With investors reluctant to commit after the turbulence of the last few days, the market was likely to keep sullenly tracking the Bund future into the year end, another dealer said.
U.S. consumer price data in the afternoon failed to inspire the market, despite being widely perceived as benign.
"We might see some buying interest if there is still some cash around, but I really don't know when that will emerge," the broker said.

Dutch bonds did manage to narrowly outperform the German market once again, as EMU worries ahead of the Dublin summit weighed on Bunds. The 10-year yield discount to Bunds ticked out another basis point, to stand at six from three on Tuesday.
The yield curve continued to steepen at the short end, with the 2-10 year spread widening to 237 basis points from 235 on Wednesday. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
